utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Good morning. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen; good morning to the technical booth, the interpreters. Are they there? Yes. Thank you. Good morning to the legal assistants, court reporters, the accused. I think the appearances are the same as on Friday. I see that Mr. Tosic is there. Good morning to the accused as well. We are going to resume our case, Kvocka and others. I hope we have all had a good rest so we can work well today. I address myself to Witness AJ. Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you had a good rest too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you have a pleasant weekend here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did. It was a nice sunny day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, quite exceptional. That is why everyone was very worried on Friday when the possibility of working on Saturday was raised. So you're now going to answer questions put to you by Madam Hollis. I wish to remind you, Witness, that you are still under oath. Madam Hollis, the floor is yours to continue with the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Hollis: [Cont'd]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AJ, when we concluded this session on Friday, you had been providing the Judges with evidence concerning certain personnel in Omarska camp that you had known before the war and before your detention in that camp. I'd like to now ask you some questions about the condition of the detainees you observed in the camp, and also the conditions of the camp itself. First of all, during your detention in Omarska camp, did you know any of the other detainees prior to being brought to the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of those detainees that you knew prior to being brought to the camp, what was the ethnicity of those detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking to you about the detainees, not the camp personnel.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. They were Muslim and Croat ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during the time you were held in Omarska camp, how often, if ever, did you observe bruising or other injuries on the detainees in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every day. Every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe for the Court the kind of bruising or injuries you observed on these detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: People were beaten with sticks, with boots, with rifle butts. It depended how frequently. Over their bodies, chest, back, arms, head, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of this, what did you observe on their bodies as a result of these beatings, what kinds of injuries or bruising?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were black and blue, and there were wounds and bruises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you began to see such bruising and such injuries how soon after you had been brought to the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the very first day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These people that you saw with these bruises and these injuries, when, if ever, did you see these persons given any kind of medical care for this bruising and injuries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see anyone giving that kind of assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the period that you were detained in Omarska, how often, if ever, did you hear sounds as of someone in pain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard moans. "Ah, oh, what am I doing here? What have I done to deserve this?" and that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How soon after you arrived in the camp did you begin to hear these kinds of sounds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those sounds and screams of pain could be heard from the first day. And when the interrogations started upstairs, when people were taken upstairs and when this was to happen, people fled from one end of the room to the other to avoid it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that when interrogations began you could hear it from upstairs. Upstairs in what building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same building in which I was detained, the building of the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that you arrived at Omarska on the 30th of May. When was the first time you received food after your arrival at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: After two days, I think. Two or three after our arrival.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after that time, after your second or third day, how often did you get food?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We got food every day, but it was not possible for everyone to get a meal. Either there was water missing or bread or food, until the next time a meal was cooked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the quality of the food that you received?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was terrible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of food did you receive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was beans and cabbage, but it was of very poor quality. You would get a small quantity of beans. You get it hot. You have to swallow it up in a minute, and there's not really anything to eat. You get one-eighth of a loaf of bread every day, sometimes once in two days. Sometimes there was electricity, sometimes there wasn't, so no cooking could be done. Bread could not be baked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself ever observe detainees being physically abused as they would go to or from their meal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did you observe this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever we went to get lunch, you'd get a blow. For instance, we would go in groups of 30, and then we would have three minutes to get there, to eat, and to come back, and to get a blow with a rifle butt, a kick. It depended. This is what I personally experience.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And based on your observation and experience, on what shifts did this kind of abuse occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one couldn't say that it was one particular shift that was better than another in its treatment. In fact, there was one shift they said, of which Milojica was the leader, was a good shift. Mujo would say, "Come on, go out. Go out." But I couldn't be bothered sometimes. I didn't leave. Then I went out, and as soon as I went out, then somebody said, "You must all go to the pista." And we sat down there, and then Simo Kevic came. He said something to the guards. I don't know what. Muharem Murselovic was in front of me. He hit him with a stick on the back. When he saw me, so he said, "Look, (redacted) is there too." Then he started beating (redacted). And then I said after that, "There won't be any good shifts any more." So I hid. I avoided going out altogether.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that you were told or that people said that one shift, of which Milojica was the leader, was a good shift. Milojica who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milojica, Krle. Krle. That's, I think, what they called him. Yes, Kos. Kos. Milojica Kos. That was his shift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Milojica Kos, Krle, did you know him before you went to the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you were in the camp, did you come to know and recognise him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in passing, as he passed by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was it that you came to know and recognise him in passing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He often wore --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I think the witness says sunglasses.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: And people said he was good. But I never had any contact with him. However, as I was beaten on the back by a member of his shift, I couldn't really agree that it was a good shift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say that you knew you were beaten by a member of his shift. How did you know that this person was on his shift?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know which shift those persons belonged to. Whether it was his shift or another shift, I don't know. But that day I was beaten, anyway, when he was part of the shift. And whether he was the leader of the shift, I don't know. For me, all of them were leaders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "all of them were leaders," what do you mean? To whom are you referring?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: All those who were in uniform, who were armed, who were in the camp, from the commanders down, whether it was Milojica, or Krkan, or Prcac, or Kvocka, or Radic. Any one of them. There were a lot of them anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that you were held in Mujo's room for a time. When you were held in that room, how many detainees were being held in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were between 700, 750, something like that. Between 700 and 750.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much space did you have in that room to move about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one couldn't really move around. Space was enough for you to lie down, and then legs were right next to one another. We lay on our sides, if I can put it that way. I couldn't lie down on my back. Somebody would have to get up for me to be able to lie on my back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in these crowded conditions, if you had to go to the toilet to relieve yourself, how were you able to move about and do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we had to step over people's legs. Sometimes you would actually step on somebody's leg to reach the toilet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you were in Mujo's room, where were the toilet facilities located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the restaurant, inside. All these rooms were in one sort of building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the conditions of the toilets in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three toilets. One of them was stopped up, and then the others would get stopped up too. And sometimes there was faeces 20 to 30 centimetres high. So sometimes bricks would be laid down for us to be able to go to the toilet. It was dreadful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the crowded conditions of this room, what was the effects of the conditions in the toilet? What was the effects of these conditions on the people in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost all of them had dysentery, all of those who were in Mujo's room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've also indicated that you were in the garage for a period of time. When you were in the garage, how many people were in there with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 136 to 140. I was there for three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how much room did you have to move about in the garage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you pull out one leg -- and we were all standing -- it was impossible to put it down again. Maybe the area was 20 to 25 square metres in all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what was the temperature like when you were inside this garage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was so hot that the walls were sticky.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself suffer any effects from the temperature and the crowding in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I fainted once. I was close to the garage door, so they beat on the door. The guard came to see what was happening, and then they said that I was sick. So he said, "Put him outside." So I spent an hour in front of the garage. When I came to, I went back inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in the garage, how were you able to get water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would get water through the small window, in a jerrycan. They would throw in this can through the window, and who manages to catch it, then the person has a drink, and what is left over is shared by the others, but all of them couldn't get enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often would they throw a jerrycan in through the window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the three days I was there, I remember that we got this jerrycan of water twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many jerrycans would they throw in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: One each time, one of ten litres each.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were held in this garage, how were you able to relieve yourselves? What toilet facilities did you have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had a barrel that was sort of cut in half, so we used that when we had to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the size of this barrel that you used, this half barrel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a 200-kilogramme barrel, maybe a hundred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was the barrel that was cut in half?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you have to empty this barrel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two people would carry it out, empty it, and bring it back in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who would be the people who would carry it out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: People from amongst us who were detained in the garage.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, when I move to this next topic, we'll need to go into private session. I'm prepared to move into that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We're going into private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Ms. Hollis, we are in public session, and you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you first arrived in Omarska, how would you describe your general physical condition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you left Omarska, how would you describe your general physical condition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Catastrophic. I left with only 49 kilos, and I had 85 or 86 when I entered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you first arrived at Omarska, how would you describe the general physical condition of the detainees that you saw there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Omarska, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, just like me. They looked like me. Everybody looked as terrible as I did. There wasn't a single man who hadn't lost 20 or 30 kilos in the process.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are you speaking about when you left the camp this was their condition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of when you first arrived at the camp, what was the general physical condition of the detainees in the camp that you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was all right. All of them were healthy and had had enough food to eat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've testified about seeing abuse of other detainees and seeing signs of abuse. You've testified about the physical abuse you yourself suffered. During the time you were in Omarska, did you ever see any camp personnel intervene to stop abuse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time you were held in Omarska, did you ever see anything to indicate to you that abusers were punished?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you leave Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th of August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did it take you to arrive at Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we left in the afternoon at about half past three, 4.00, and we were there at around 12.00 half past twelve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you left Omarska camp, before you left the camp, did you recognise any camp personnel present as you were leaving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The day that you left Omarska camp, as you were preparing to leave and as you were leaving, did you recognise any camp personnel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, all of them. The ones that were with me. There were 176 of us, I think, who were called out that day, in three buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say you were called out. Who was calling you out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether it was Krivaja or someone else -- it was one of the guards, at any rate. Whether it was Krivaja or Brk or someone else, I don't really know, because I didn't even like to look much. They would just call your name out and you went where you had to go. You didn't do much looking around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were outside, before you were put on the buses, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when we went there, I had a bottle of water with me, a litre and a half in a plastic bottle. That's what I took with me from Omarska, so that it was handy in the bus, because it was very hot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this bus that you were put on, how many people were on the bus with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were -- we were lined up like matches, 50 or 60 of us. We all had to lie down. We weren't able to sit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how crowded was the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was overcrowded. Twenty or 30 people more than the bus could carry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the detainees, were there any other individuals on the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were. There were the guards. The driver of the bus, the guard. I was in the middle of the bus, and the bus was one of the articulated types. No. That is to say, it had a door in the middle and that's where I was. I bent down, took this bottle of water that I had with me, so that I didn't raise my head up much to avoid being seen or heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The guard that was on the bus, did you recognise this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the conditions --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't looking. I wasn't looking, actually, because this wasn't a time for looking around, as I say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the conditions like on the bus during this bus trip?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were terrible as well. We had to relieve ourselves there, both to pass a stool and to urinate, because there was no way of going out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during this bus trip to Manjaca, how often, if ever, did the bus-stop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It stopped fairly frequently. I can't tell you exactly the number of times, whether it was five times or six times or ten times, but it did stop along the way. And often when it did stop, there would be beatings there too. And if somebody had any money on him, they would look. If they had watches or any other valuables, any gold jewellery, he would ask for that. And if he searched you and found anything on you which you hadn't -- then he would kill you. So we all gave up all what we had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, upon your arrival at Manjaca, did you immediately go into the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were there until 6.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the night while you were there, how many people, if any, were called off the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my bus, only one person was called, and he was Dedo Crnalic, my neighbour. He also had a private premises. He was a tailor, in fact, in a small catering establishment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after he was called off the bus, what, if anything, did you hear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard moans and a scream and fighting, struggle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Dedo Crnalic again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning. When they killed him, they brought him back. When he was beaten -- they had beaten him -- they brought him back to the bus, to the front door of the bus, and in the morning at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw him in the morning at 6.00, what was his condition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dead. He lay there. He lay three metres away from me, three or four metres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, if we could go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We're going to move into private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in public session now. You may continue, Madam Hollis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AJ, during your testimony you have mentioned Kvocka. Would you be able to recognise Kvocka today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If he's present in the courtroom, would you please point to him and identify him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He has thinning hair. He's wearing a blue suit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is he located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see him on the screen. He's sitting to my left, just below the glass window.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, there are several individuals sitting there. Would you please tell us where he is among those individuals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is number three. He is the third in line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Starting with whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is the third both from the left and counting from the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what individuals are you counting here? Would you please tell us the first individual you are counting? What is that individual wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Krkan, Kvocka, Milojica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of clothing are those individuals wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see from here it looks like blue, with a tie, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are any of those --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: A blue shirt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned a Milojica. Where is Milojica sitting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's the second, counting from the right, sitting right next to Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned Krkan. Where is Krkan sitting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's the first on the left-hand side, next to Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you also mentioned Prcac and Zigic. Would you be able to identify them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm looking straight at Prcac, and he's looking at me, and Zigic is next to him, next to Prcac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is Prcac sitting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's sitting in the front row.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Zigic, you said, is sitting next to him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the front row, on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam Hollis. For the Defence, Mr. Krstan Simic. What is the order going to be? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in view of the fact that we had a shorter testimony than we expected, we haven't been able to consult about the cross-examination. Many things were mentioned for the first time. So perhaps it would be best to proceed in the order of the indictment, and in the case that one of the Defence counsel does not have any questions, he will be able to say so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It means that you will be beginning, Mr. Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please proceed. Witness AJ, you are now going to answer questions which Mr. Krstan Simic is going to put to you. He is the Defence counsel for one of the accused. Cross-examined by Mr. K. Simic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness AJ.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, I wish to express my regret because of everything that you've been through. I shall try and be as brief as possible, and I shall begin from your stay in the Omarska camp. You said that you were accommodated in three different places or, rather, four, the "white house," the pista, the garage, and the so-called Mujo's room. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific regarding where you were in which location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be able to be specific regarding days and hours, that is not possible because those were not the times when you paid attention to such things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't expect that, but just approximately. When you arrived in Omarska, where were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Mujo's room, as it was called.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some 50 days, perhaps, combined with the pista. I stayed at the pista maybe five or six days. You would go out; then you would come back. In the "white house" I stayed, again, two or three times, I think. In the garage, I was there for three days prior to leaving for Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AJ, let us focus on the first 20 days of your detention. Could you be more specific for that period regarding your exact location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In those 20 or so days, I was both in Mujo's room and at the pista. Because it was so hot during the daytime, you would spend time on the pista, and then in the evening, in Mujo's room, and back and forth. One sought to find some sort of shelter, as far as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago you said that, in view of the circumstances, you avoided --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first ten days or so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you hid so as not to go out. So that was during the first ten-day period.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After being beaten by Zoran Zigic, I tried to hide, but that really didn't depend on me. If I went for lunch, I would be visible, everyone else would see me, by the guards, for instance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AJ, do you know who was in charge of the preparation of food in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AJ, do you know who was in charge of organising the hygiene, or rather to maintain hygienic conditions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any cleaning ladies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I saw, I saw nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that first 10-day period, or rather 20-day period, in the compound was there a unit for some other purpose?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your testimony you mentioned that during your interrogation, when you were beaten up, that the interrogator was somebody called Horvat.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's not from Banja Luka. But with Horvat was his colleague from Banja Luka. No, Milan Hrvacanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then this is an error. "Horvat" should be "Hrvacanin"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Hrvacanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My last question. After the beating in the "white house" that you have described, did Bato Kovacevic ask you what happened to you? I'm sure you know him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't. Bato did come there two or three times, I think, but on that particular day, or the next day, he didn't come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Simic. Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence team of the second accused has no questions for Witness AJ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Mr. Nikolic. Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before I begin, are we in public session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, we are in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the witness mentioned his nickname twice while we were in public session, and this could be a risk for his identity. So could that be checked? That is in the interests of all around, not in my personal interest. I think he mentioned his nickname. I don't want to repeat it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Fila, for drawing my attention to that. (redacted). (redacted). Mr. Dubuisson, we need to have that redacted. But I'm not sure whether we were then or are now in public session or private session. Please take note of that, Mr. Dubuisson, and make the necessary redactions. Mr. Fila, you may continue. Thank you very much. Cross-examined by Mr. Fila:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have your nice name, so I don't want to call you by AJ. I'll just say "sir" instead. Do you know where Mr. Murselovic is now, whom you mentioned now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is he now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vice-president of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he goes to work regularly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you knew certain persons, apart from Milojica Kos, who is not from Prijedor. May I ask you why, in your earlier statements, you didn't mention any of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have plenty to say and to mention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should like to ask you something else. Since you said "They all came to have haircuts in your shop," you were acquaintances with some, you were even friends, may I ask you the following: Did you see at the same time together Radic, Prcac, Kvocka, Kos? Did you see them at the same time and in the same place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All four of them together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you perhaps remember, when you arrived on the 30th of May, you came with Beganovic and the others; right? If I understood you correctly. If not, please correct me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We arrived on the same day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the guards receive you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which shift was on duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Never mind. Never mind. In answer to a question from the Prosecutor, you said that they were all, for you, bosses and that you didn't know who held which position. Did you by any chance see any one of them issuing orders? Specifically Mr. Radic, did you see him issuing orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Praemonitas, praemonitus. Since you said you knew them, did you address any one of them individually for assistance, for aid, or did you complain to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only that one time when I went to Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. That's all I have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Fila. Thank you very much. Mr. Tosic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have only one request. As we are approaching the break, if possible, could we have the break first so that I can consult with my client and start the cross-examination after the break? Because we have very little time until the break. I apologise. Maybe my colleague Jovan Simic could cross-examine until the break -- he is Defence counsel for Mr. Prcac -- to make the best of the time. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have one question, so we could take it until the break, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. I still haven't got the translation. If I understood correctly, Mr. Tosic would like to reverse the order. So it will now be Mr. Jovan Simic who would like to do the cross-examination. Is that correct, Mr. Tosic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, Mr. Jovan Simic, you now have the floor for the cross-examination, if you please. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] May I begin?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, you have the floor. You may begin. Cross-examined by Mr. J. Simic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I should like to ask you, you mentioned the case when (redacted) was killed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the details of that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was lunchtime. We were sitting on the pista.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you sitting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the pista.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between the hangar and -- MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. Could the witness point out the exact position that he held at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there will be some difficulty, but let's see. I think not. Mr. Dubuisson.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have to go into closed session to be able to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, you've got the answer. For the witness to be able to get up, we have to go into closed session. Is that what you want, Mr. Jovan Simic? MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Yes, if you would kindly agree. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's go into closed session. Mr. Usher, will you please pull down the curtains.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we're in public session now. We're going to have a break of half an hour, after which we will resume with the cross-examination by Mr. Tosic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated. We shall continue where we left off in the cross-examination of the Witness AJ, and I should like to mention that we have Mr. Michael Keegan with us. Mr. Tosic, you were the next. You may begin, Mr. Tosic. Cross-exam by Mr. Tosic:

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one moment, please, to get my things together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I ask the questions, I should like to show the Witness AJ -- that is to say, the Defence and our client would like to express our condolences for all the suffering he experienced in 1992 in Omarska, but life goes on, and here are our questions. I should like the witness to answer a question. If he considers that he does not wish to answer it or for any personal reasons he need not give an answer, but that question relates to the following: In his testimony, he says that he was -- when he did his regular military service, he was proclaimed unfit for military service and discharged. Can he tell us please, today, what the reasons were for his being discharged from the army, from the medical aspects, his health? What was the reason for which he did not have to do his regular military service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I was flat-footed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The second question is the following: Could you tell us whether before the war you were a member of any party; that is to say, before you came to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you were not a member of any political party, could you tell us whether in the course of 1991 and perhaps in 1992 you may have given financial assistance to the members of any party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Do you happen to know Nihad Haskic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how you came know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a neighbour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what his business was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had mechanical building equipment, and he also had a catering business selling Cevapcici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether in the period prior to the beginning of the war whether this person bought any weapons or dealt in any illegal trade of any kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know Sead Dzuzin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you happen to know him and how long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know him from the town. He worked in the town planning institute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember, as a citizen of Prijedor, in the course of the first half of 1992, an incident which occurred, that is to say, which was caused by Sead Dzuzin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your testimony today, you said that Zoran Zigic -- that you hardly new Zoran Zigic before the war.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you explained to the Trial Chamber about Saponja, Dusan Knezevic, and Nikica Janjic, that you knew them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us briefly how you knew them, how long you had known them, and you came to know them before the war, these three individuals? We can take them individually, one by one. How long have you known Nikica Janjic, and how did you come to meet him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have known Nikica for eight or nine years. He was at the seaside with me, at this holiday camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Saponja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Saponja had a flat in Titova Street. We would meet every day. He would come to my shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Knezevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know Knezevic very well, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you explain to us whether, before coming to Omarska, at any time you had any conflict of any kind, dispute of any kind, or some unsettled accounts, perhaps, with Knezevic, Saponja, and Janjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came to Omarska, you said that in the incident that occurred, that is to say, when you were beaten, that Zigic, Saponja, Knezevic, and Janjic took part in this. Could you explain to us, apart from that incident whether you were, at any time after that, while you were in Omarska, happened to see Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before this incident or after this particular incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that incident then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw him then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what I'm asking you is whether you saw Zigic Zoran before this incident at any time in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Zoran Zigic after the incident, up to the time you left Omarska? Did you ever see him again in Omarska during your stay there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now go back to the incident I mentioned earlier on. You said that Zoran Zigic called out your name when you were in the restaurant, before you went to the "white house."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was with him? Was he alone when you went from the restaurant towards the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. He was alone. And who was with you? Were you alone or was someone else with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Hasan just ran up to me, and all this happened in those five or six or ten metres. In the space of -- in that space.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to us where (redacted) was and Emir Beganovic? Where were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the "white house."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they come before, afterwards, or together with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before me. I came last.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who took them off?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was Nikica there, Duca as well. They were in this group, sort of group. Duca, Knezevic, Saponja, Nikica Janjic, Zigic. There was another man. I don't remember his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us just go back for a moment and clarify something. You say that (redacted) and Emir Beganovic, that they were already in the "white house."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that or did you just hear about that? Did you hear about who took them off and how long before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, everything took place in the space of four or five minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you remember who took them off?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was just one roll-call when Zigic asked for the men, Kiki, and before Kiki, Beganovic, (redacted), and Asaf went out. They left before me. Whether it was five minutes before me or six minutes, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who took them off? Who took them from the restaurant to the "white house"? Did you happen to see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, tell us this: When you were in the "white house," which room were you in exactly as you go into the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the left-hand side there is one room, and from that room you enter into another room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was it the first room or the second room on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first. Thank you. In that room were you alone or were you there with someone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted) was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who else was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slavko Ecimovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anybody else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I was just fighting for myself, so I can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether in that particular room, together with you, was Emir Beganovic there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't remember. Very well. After leaving the room in the "white house," did you happen to see Emir Beganovic and --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw him, did you see whether he had been in your room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was coming out of the "white house."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you remember whether he was together with you in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for me it's all one room. There was no door. So we were in the same room, the five of us. Now, whether he was in the front part or in the back part, I can't say, but it all took place in the "white house."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. But explain to us once again. You said you were beaten by Knezevic, Saponja, and Zigic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe to us what Zigic looked like, what he was wearing, and whether you noticed anything unusual on him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing a uniform. He had a red beret. Duca was wearing an olive-green one, as far as I remember. Saponja, I couldn't really say what kind of clothes he was wearing, because it was a fight for survival, for life itself, so I didn't think about things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what Zigic beat you with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: With his fists, with his shoes, with his baton, club, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you perhaps remember who beat you when your tooth fell out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well the two of them, Duca and Zoran Zigic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And linked to your teeth, after you left the camp, did you go to a medical institution for medical help, medical assistance, whether in Yugoslavia or outside Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside the territory of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left the "white house," you said, in your testimony, that Zigic told you that you drink water -- that you should, like pigs.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that we should wash ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Do you remember whether that was what he said or might he have said something similar to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a hundred per cent. That is what I heard him say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody ride on your back from the "white house" to the pista?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not me. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody make you drink motor oil?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to recall when they went out with you, that is to say, (redacted), Asaf Kapetanovic, Emir Beganovic, did anybody order them to drink motor oil or did anybody ride on their backs? Did you happen to see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see it, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that on several occasions, that is say, five, that you were beaten when you -- while you were interrogated.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you said that you never saw Zoran Zigic again in Omarska after that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see him, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about -- that is to say, do you know Becir Meduljanin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he's not there. He's not here any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have one more question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to us -- you said about Meduljanin, that he's not here any more. Did you happen to see him after you left the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw him only when he arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one further question. Can you perhaps remember, looking back at the "white house," whether you noticed any bandages and on what arm of Zoran Zigic? Did he have a bandage of any kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Tosic. Madam Hollis, do you have any questions, additional ones?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead. Re-examined by Ms. Hollis:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified that after the beating in the white house by Zigic, you tried to hide. You also testified that after that beating, you went to Mujo's room. After you went to back to Mujo's room, after having received that beating, when did you next leave Mujo's room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps after five or six days. Five or six days later, I went upstairs for an interrogation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were asked if you ever saw Radic, Prcac, Kvocka, and Kos all together --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- and you testified that you did.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see Kvocka, Radic, Prcac, and Kos all together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you saw them all together at Omarska, what do you mean by that? All in the same location at the same time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. There was a lot of other space. There were the hangars, the garages, the restaurant, Mujo's room, as they referred to it. They couldn't all be together at the same time. One was in one place, another one was somewhere else, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also asked if you ever complained to any of these people or asked their aid, and you indicated that, except for this one occasion with Kvocka, you neither complained nor asked their aid. Now, why did you never complain or ask for aid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't worth it because there was no aid. It was the same for everyone, and so there was no point. And I didn't see him -- I couldn't see that anybody could help anybody or make it easier for anyone, except for that once when I asked not to be in the "green house" but in the restaurant, and he permitted that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By "he," you mean who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean Miroslav Kvocka. I'm thinking of Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Madam Hollis. Judge Riad has the floor. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness AJ. I apologise for not referring to you by your real name. I should like to know, if you can tell me, that is to say, I'd like you to specify some points to help me understand better what you said during your testimony. You spoke about Mr. Kvocka and you said that he authorised you -- you had a little piece of paper and he let you go to Mujo's room, if I understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said that it was very near. Now, there are two ways of looking at this: Because it was very near, because it was near, he could have given you this permit, or because he was the individual who had the authority to grant you permission. Could you clarify that? Was it just because he was around, or was he the authority who could only issue a permit of this kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I left the interrogation, I can't remember which guard was at the door, but I asked whether I could go into Mujo's room and he said, no, the "green house," that is to say, the pista. And I said, "Well, could I go there?" and he said, "Well, there's Kvocka and Kvocka can say whether you can or not." So for me, Kvocka was the person in charge at the time, and he gave me this chit, piece of paper, which allowed me to go to Mujo's room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but in your testimony you said that they were all -- I'm repeating what you said -- they were all number one, all leaders, speaking about Kos, Kvocka, Zigic, et cetera. Well, then, on the basis of this incident, Kvocka seemed to be in greater authority, to have more authority than the others.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for me, he did have more authority because that's what the guard said to me who was there. He said that I should go and see with him and that he was on the pista. And so it was easier for me; I went to him straight away, when the guards told me that. And he said, "Just wait a second," and he wrote this piece of paper for me and then I returned to Mujo's room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So he had more authority than the others, is that it? In your opinion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at that particular moment, he did, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. All the accused that you've indicated just now and identified, were they all near the interrogation room where people were moving around? Were they on the same floor? Were they interrogating?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know. There was another team, another group, who was doing the investigation from Banja Luka, from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With respect to Mr. Kos, you said two things which seemed to me to be a little irreconcilable; that is to say, you said that he was all right but that his group mistreated you and beat you and that he wasn't able to stop his group from beating you. If he was a nice man, if he was kind. Or didn't he have any authority over them? How do you reconcile those two statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps in my case, I didn't -- it didn't happen to me, what was actually going on. But he seemed to be rather nice towards me. He had glasses on; he had put up his trouser legs. I didn't really know him but he just seemed to be okay towards me. I knew him better from the people -- that is to say, I heard about him from the people who knew him better than me. Murho Kapetanovic knew him, and so on, so I heard about him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but he didn't intervene to prevent them from abusing you, from mistreating you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't feel that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said that nonetheless he was a nice man, that he was nice towards you. About Mr. Zigic now, he asked you for money, 100.000 marks, German marks. Did you owe him any money? Why did he ask you? Amongst all the other prisoners, why did he choose you, to ask money of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know why he asked me in particular but he probably assumed that I had some money. And I didn't have the money on me, in my tracksuit, so I didn't have the money.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it was because of your reputation and not an old debt that he wanted to settle, or anything of that kind.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At one particular moment you said that there was an incident, a regrettable incident, where (redacted), who was eating, was killed because he said to the guard "Bujrum," for simply saying "Bujrum" to him. Could you kill anybody at any time like that, without any orders, without anyone stopping them, or was it because of the interrogation or something? What was your impression of the killing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the killing, you could kill somebody in the space of 24 hours, whenever they wanted to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this killing was the order of the day, so to speak. Anybody could kill, is that right, depending on the caprice of the guards, the whims of the guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course, it depended where you were. If you were close -- if they could see you and you were close to them, then you would run the risk of running into that kind of trouble rather than if you were further away from them, out of sight, sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So what purpose did the interrogations serve? To see whether somebody was more guilty or less guilty? Why the interrogation if people could be killed anyway at random, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't the classical type of killing. Something had to happen; there had to be a reason of some kind why. For example, they interrogated me about this truckload of weapons, and this had nothing to do with anything, with any weapons. But they wrote something down, they took note of something, and that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it was a sort of scenario.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What about the guards? The guards that you recognised, did they have nicknames? You mentioned nicknames. Could you tell us, state clearly, what each of their nicknames were, what each of their nicknames were in the camp? Could you give us all their nicknames?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the ones here, you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Krkan, his nickname was Krkan. Radic Mladjo, Krkan, and I know him as Krkan and I've known him to be Krkan for the past 20 years. Kvocka, well. Milojica Kos, I didn't know him; I got to know him in Omarska. Prcac, Drago, well, I knew him, he knew me, because I went to the SUP; I had a lot of friends there. That kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question, perhaps you're unable to answer it. But looking back now, who was the most important in the camp, in your opinion? Every institution has somebody who has more authority than others.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to my mind, at that time, it was Kvocka, perhaps because he did me this service. So in my opinion, he was the superior. And as for the others, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The others, were they of the same nature and the same rank? They could do what they wanted, couldn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could. They could do what they wanted, yes, because they had control of everything around them. They were colleagues, friends, working together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those that you described as being kind, they could intervene to prevent something happening to others, to show a certain degree of mercy, of compassion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You didn't notice it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Thank you, Witness AJ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge Riad. Judge Wald.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Witness AJ, I have only two brief questions. During the whole time that you were at Omarska, did anyone ever tell you and the people around you, the other detainees, what was going to happen to you? I mean, how long you might be held, whether you would be released, and if so, for what reason you would be released, where you would go? Did you or the other people have any idea what was going to happen to you during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no idea what would happen, but I was always afraid of the worst. And I can't say that I heard from anyone where we might go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I'm sure that you and the detainees around you must have talked together and worried together. What did the other people around you, the detainees, think was going to happen? You said you were always afraid of the worst. What does "the worst" mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Getting killed, being called out and then you wouldn't know whether you would come back or not. There were some people who never came back; others came back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So it wasn't until August, when you were removed to the other camp, that you had any idea what was going to happen to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. My other question is: During the beating in which Zigic was there and participated, after you'd had the conversation about money and you were actually in the "white house," and before you were taken out again for the drinking of the water episode, did Zigic say anything to you about the reason for the beating or ask you any questions, or did he -- in other words, did he verbalise, did he say anything to you, during the beating? Not the money part before or the water afterwards.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: No. Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Nikolic. We haven't finished yet. You have an important question to raise? Thank you. I have a little question for you, a very simple one. When you were arrested, the person or persons who arrested you, did they explain to you why you were being arrested? Did they give you any reasons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another aspect of the same question. Did you understand, did you have any idea of the reasons behind it at that moment? Did you have any understanding why you were being arrested at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simply because I was a Muslim; that was my impression.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Thank you very much, Witness AJ. We have finished with our questions. Mr. Nikolic, you have something to say before the witness leaves?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I apologise, but the Defence of the accused finds itself in the same situation that my colleague Fila was in on Friday. His Honour Judge Riad, addressing questions to the witness, asked, among other things, whether the accused Kos could intervene. Regarding the incident that occurred to the witness at the pista, he never mentioned the presence of the accused Kos there, so I don't see how he could have intervened if he didn't see him and if he was not present -- and I think that is what can be seen from the transcript -- and that the witness clearly said that he didn't know which shift the guards that mistreated him belonged to. I'm not talking about ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nikolic, you can't cross-examine now. We have finished. The question that you have raised --

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not cross-examining, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but the witness was speaking to you. So the question that you raised will be entered in the record. We are still considering this matter. And for the moment, I think it is all going into the record and we can see from the record what the witness said on one occasion and what he said on the next occasion. You yourself can draw your conclusions at the end of the proceedings, or you can present evidence to prove the contrary. If, at every moment, we are making allegations, we will totally upset the Rules. You have the transcript, which says this and that, and you can analyse it and draw your conclusions in your final statement, in your brief, and present evidence to prove whatever you wish to prove.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in my notes, this team was the Kos team, called Krle. If I am mistaken, I think we need to check straight away. These are notes taken from the translation. Krle is Kos, is it not? And in my notes, it said that it was his shift. Krle is Kos, isn't he? So in my notes, it says "Krle's shift." That is why I asked for the nicknames, because we're a little confused because sometimes nicknames are used and sometimes proper names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much. The question is closed. The transcript speaks for itself. You can make your own conclusions. At the end you can present your own evidence. So we don't have to go back to this whole issue now. Witness AJ, you have finished your testimony here. The Prosecution has had questions for you, the Defence has also had questions for you, and the Judges have asked you questions. Do you have anything you wish to state that was not asked of you, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. We have no exhibits to deal with. So I think, because of the protective measures for the witness, we have to pull down the curtains so that the witness can leave, and when he leaves, I shall give the floor to Mr. Tosic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. I have a question for the witness, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. Tosic. You're an attorney. You know very well that at this stage of the proceedings you have no right to ask the witness any questions. You are an attorney, aren't you, Mr. Tosic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation] But there are concessions sometimes, and I am sorry too, but, you know, there are limits to those concessions, and there must be order and we must respect the rules. Madam Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution has conferred with the Defence. The Defence has no objection. The next witness that the Prosecution will be calling is Mr. Oklopcic, and he will be testifying in open session, with no protective measures. And, Your Honour, Mr. Keegan will be leading this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Keegan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I'm informed there is some difficulty with the witness. He is just outside the door, but apparently there may be some confusion with his status. So if I could have leave to go find out exactly what it is he's asking for or speaking about. If I could have leave for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Keegan. So long as you don't go to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Oklopcic. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you have to run a lot? Have you been running?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You are now going to read the solemn declaration, which the usher is going to give you, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you comfortable?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Very much so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, could you lower the microphones of the witness and switch on both microphones, please. Now, the examination-in-chief will be conducted by Mr. Keegan.
